title: Node.get_path_to() use_unique_path does not work when called on target's owner
body: ### Tested versions Reproducible in: - v4.7.2.rc1.official [36a04fe52] ### System information Godot v4.7.2.rc1 - Bluefin 44.20260811 (Silverblue) on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 1 monitor - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - AMD Radeon 860M Graphics (radeonsi, krackan1, ACO, DRM 3.64, 7.0.12-201.fc44.x86_64) - AMD Ryzen AI 7 PRO 350 w/ Radeon 860M (16 threads) - 58.49 GiB memory - PulseAudio (44100 Hz, Stereo/mono) ### Issue description `Node.get_path_to()` has an optional `use_unique_path: bool` parameter, documented as follows: > If `use_unique_path` is `true`, returns the shortest path accounting for this node's unique name (see `unique_name_in_owner`). `Node.unique_name_in_owner` says (emphasis mine): > If `true`, the node can be accessed from any node sharing the same `owner` or **from the `owner` itself**, with special `%Name` syntax in `get_node()`. From this, if you have `node` with `name` set to `Foo` and `unique_name_in_owner` set to `true`, I would expect `node.owner.get_path_to(node, true)` to return `^"%Foo"`. However, it does not: it returns a relative path to `node`. ### Steps to reproduce For example, set up this scene: with set `Access as Unique Name` on C. Attach a script to A with the following code to see the paths from each node to C with `use_unique_path` set to `true`: ```gdscript extends Node func _ready() -> void: prints("path from A to C", self .get_path_to(%C, true)) # "B1/C" - wrong, this is a longer path than %C prints("path from B1 to C", $B1 .get_path_to(%C, true)) # ^"%C" - correct prints("path from C to C", %C .get_path_to(%C, true)) # ^"." - OK, no longer than %C prints("path from D to C", %C/D .get_path_to(%C, true)) # ^".." - Tolerable, no longer than %C prints("path from E to C", %C/D/E .get_path_to(%C, true)) # ^"../.." - I think this is also wrong, %C is shorter prints("path from B2 to C", $B2 .get_path_to(%C, true)) # ^"%C" - correct``` ``` Given that the path from B1 (parent of C) to C is `%C`, but also the path from B2 (C's "aunt") to C is `%C`, I think the path from A to C should also be `%C`. (I also think the paths from C's children back up to C should also be `%C`; in particular the path given from C's grandchild to C is longer than `%C`.) ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) [get-path-to-use-unique-path.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/31078641/get-path-to-use-unique-path.zip)
